correctness.rationale: Surface Riemann-Roch gives the displayed bilinear form in the invariants (rank,c1,chi). A closed point, the adjusted structure-sheaf class and adjusted line-bundle classes surject integrally onto the three summands; nondegeneracy of the target form makes the kernel exactly the numerical radical. In the resulting basis the Euler matrix has blocks (-c,1), canonical-intersection vector k, and -Q; reordering and the stated integral row and column operations transform it exactly to H direct-sum (-Q). The Hodge index sign then makes the determinant positive. Fresh symbolic checking of the formula and the packaged exact matrix reduction confirms the Smith-factor consequence on independent nonsingular test lattices.

originality.rationale: Liu-Shen-Zhang introduce the numerical Cartan determinant and prove positivity in broad geometric classes but their public primary statement does not give the all-surface integral determinant formula. Krah's full open article gives the surface Riemann-Roch Euler form and only a rational Chern-character identification K_num,Q with Q plus Pic_num,Q plus Q; it develops the Neron-Severi pseudolattice but does not state the integral Smith normal form. Vial's results relate maximal numerical exceptional collections to Neron-Severi unimodularity under additional hypotheses. Resultary search returned no distinct theorem with the full discriminant-group identification.

value.rationale: The current Cartan-determinant program asks for geometric control of the Euler determinant. In dimension two this theorem gives a complete answer and strengthens a single determinant to the entire finite cokernel, identifying exactly when numerical Euler theory is unimodular. That is a natural structural bridge between numerical K-theory and the classical Neron-Severi lattice.
residual_risks: Because the row-column reduction is elementary once the integral generators are chosen, an equivalent statement may exist in unindexed surface K-theory or lattice literature.

final_claim: For every smooth projective surface over an algebraically closed field, the numerical Grothendieck group is integrally identified by rank, first Chern class and Euler characteristic with Z plus N^1(X) plus Z, and its Euler matrix is Smith-equivalent to a hyperbolic plane plus the negative intersection matrix. Consequently its Euler cokernel is the Neron-Severi discriminant group and its determinant is the absolute Neron-Severi discriminant.
scientific_limitations: Because the row-column reduction is elementary once the integral generators are chosen, an equivalent statement may exist in unindexed surface K-theory or lattice literature.
The argument is surface-specific; higher dimensions involve additional numerical cycle lattices.
